\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Recursion}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Encoded machine relation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p005-b001}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a function from four deciders and Boolean words to truth values,
let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $s,u,v$ be natural numbers. Define $u$ to be related
to $v$ (with parameter $s$ and input $x$) exactly when decider number $3$ accepts the
encoding of $x$, the canonical binary expansions of $u$ and $v$, and the canonical
binary expansion of $s$, nested as a sequence of pairs.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Configuration invariant]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p005-b002}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St}
For natural numbers $s,w,i$ and a machine configuration $\sigma$, the invariant requires
its input-length, base, exponent, power, scratch, loop-counter, pop-scratch, and
popped-endpoint registers all to be zero. It also requires the radius to equal $s$, the
width to equal $w$, the code bound to equal $2^w$, the source and target codes to be
less than $2^w$, the midpoint to be at most $2^w$, the level to equal $i$, the endpoint
stack to be less than $2^{w(w-i)}$, and the phase stack to be less than $2^{w-i}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Exponential size bounds]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For every natural number $w$, one has $w<2^w$ and $2^w\le 2^{w^2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Register bound from the invariant]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts}
\difficulty{4}
Let $s,w,i$ be natural numbers, and let a state have natural-number registers
$n,a,X,P,T,Z,C,s_0,w_0,K,U,V,M,I,SE,SP,E,Q$. Suppose the invariant conditions hold:
$n=a=X=P=T=Z=C=Q=E=0$, $s_0=s$, $w_0=w$, $K=2^w$, $U,V<2^w$, $M\le 2^w$, $I=i$,
$SE<2^{w(w-i)}$, and $SP<2^{w-i}$. If $s\le w$ and $i\le w$, then every listed register
is at most $2^{w^2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bound for a Pushed Endpoint]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.push_lt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.push_lt}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $w,i,SE,v$, if $i+1\le w$, $SE<2^{w(w-(i+1))}$, and $v<2^w$, then
$SE\,2^w+v<2^{w(w-i)}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bound for a Pushed Phase Bit]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.pushP_lt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.pushP_lt}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $w,i,SP$, if $i+1\le w$ and $SP<2^{w-(i+1)}$, then $2SP+1<2^{w-i}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Base-Level Reachability Simulation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.base_spec}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.base_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.refl, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.vword_whole₃, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E,s,w$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean oracle with four indices and
Boolean-word inputs, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a machine
register state. Suppose $s\le w$ and $\mathrm{st}$ satisfies the level-zero invariant for
$s,w$. Then the program $A(E)$ has a finite execution from label $\mathrm{cl}$, with register
vector given by $\mathrm{st}$ and no answer, to label $\mathrm{rt}(b)$, where $b$ is the truth value
of level-zero reachability from $\mathrm{st}.U$ to $\mathrm{st}.V$ with bound $2^w$ and relation
determined by the step oracle, $x$, and $s$. Every configuration strictly before the
final one satisfies the program guard and has every register at most $2^{w^2}$; the
final register vector is unchanged from $\mathrm{st}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Recursive call correctness]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CallOK}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b001}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CallOK}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV}
Fix a natural number $E$, a four-decider Boolean-word function $\mathrm{orc}$, a Boolean
word $x$, and natural numbers $s,w$. For a natural number $i$, the call property says
that every configuration satisfying the invariant for $s,w,i$ admits a midpoint $M'\le
2^w$ such that the program starting at the recursive-call label reaches a configuration
at the return label for the truth value of bounded reachability between its source and
target at level $i$, with the midpoint register set to $M'$. This run is required to
satisfy the specified guard with bound $2^{w^2}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[First recursive descent branch]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.desc1}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b001}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.desc1}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.refl, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CallOK, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cont, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvDst, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvExit, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvSrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mv_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.pop_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.pushP_lt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.pushV_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.push_lt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.reach_of_eq}
\difficulty{6}
Let $E,s,w,i\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean oracle on four indices and
Boolean words, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a register state.
Assume $s\leq w$, $i+1\leq w$, the recursive call property holds at level $i$, the state
satisfies the level-$(i+1)$ invariant with parameters $s,w$, and its midpoint register
$M$ is strictly less than $2^w$. Then there is an $M_1\leq 2^w$ such that, starting at
the midpoint-search loop with this state, the machine reaches the phase-1 push site if
the level-$i$ reachability predicate holds from the source code $U$ to the current
midpoint $M$, and otherwise reaches the phase-0 failure site. At the end, the target
register is the old midpoint, the popped-endpoint register is the old target, and the
midpoint register is $M_1$; throughout the run all configurations satisfy the guard
bounding every register by $2^{w^2}$ and requiring valid instructions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second recursive descent branch]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.desc2}
\proofsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b001}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.desc2}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.refl, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CallOK, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cont, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvDst, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvExit, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvSrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mv_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.pop_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.pushP_lt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.pushU_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.push_lt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.reach_of_eq}
\difficulty{6}
Let $E,s,w,i\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean-valued oracle on four
indices and Boolean words, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a
register state. Suppose $s\leq w$, $i+1\leq w$, the recursive-call property holds at
level $i$, and $\mathrm{st}$ satisfies the level-$(i+1)$ invariant with parameters
$s,w$; also suppose its midpoint register is less than $2^w$ and $M_1\leq 2^w$. Starting
at phase $0$ of the push loop for the true phase bit, with the target register set to
the original midpoint, the midpoint register set to $M_1$, and the popped-endpoint
register set to the original target, the machine reaches the phase-1 success site when
level-$i$ reachability holds from the original midpoint to the original target, and the
phase-1 failure site otherwise. For some $M_2\leq 2^w$, its final source register is the
original midpoint, its midpoint register is $M_2$, and its popped-endpoint register is
the original source; every configuration before the final one satisfies the guard
requiring valid instructions and all registers at most $2^{w\cdot w}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Phase-zero failure-loop reachability]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail0F}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail0F}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvDst, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvExit, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvSrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mv_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.reach_of_eq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal O$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four indices
and each Boolean word, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $s,w\in\mathbb N$ satisfy
$s\le w$. Let $i\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $i+1\le w$, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be an
18-register machine state such that $n,a,X,P,T,Z,C,Q,E$ are all zero; $s$ and $w$ are
its radius and width, respectively; $K=2^w$; $U,V<2^w$; $M\le2^w$; $I=i+1$;
$SE<2^{w(w-(i+1))}$; and $SP<2^{w-(i+1)}$. If $M<2^w$ and $M_1\le2^w$, then there is a
finite run from the phase-zero failure label with registers given by the state obtained
from $\mathrm{st}$ by replacing $V$ with $M$, $M$ with $M_1$, and $E$ with the old value
of $V$, to the loop label with registers given by the state obtained from $\mathrm{st}$
by replacing $M$ with $M+1$; every configuration strictly before the endpoint satisfies
the guard with bound $2^{w^2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Phase-One Success Return Path]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail1T}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p005-b004,

\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail1T}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvDst, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvExit, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvSrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mv_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.reach_of_eq}
\difficulty{3}
Let $E,s,w,i$ be natural numbers with $s\le w$ and $i+1\le w$, let
$\mathrm{orc}:\mathrm{Fin}(4)\to\mathrm{List}(\mathrm{Bool})\to\mathrm{Bool}$ be an
oracle, let $x$ be a Boolean list, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a machine state satisfying
the invariant $\mathrm{Inv}(s,w,i+1,\mathrm{st})$. For every $M_2\le 2^w$, the machine
$A(E)$ has a finite run from the configuration whose control state is the phase-one
success state, whose registers agree with $\mathrm{st}$ except that $U=M$, $M=M_2$, and
$E$ equals the original value of $U$, and whose result is unset, to the configuration
whose control state is the successful return state and whose registers agree with
$\mathrm{st}$ except that $M=M_2$, again with unset result; throughout the run, every
configuration before the final one satisfies the input precondition and has all
registers at most $2^{w^2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Phase-one failure loop]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail1F}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail1F}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvDst, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvExit, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mvSrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mv_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.reach_of_eq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E$ be a natural number, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be an oracle with four indices and
Boolean-word queries, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $s,w$ be natural numbers with
$s\le w$. Let $i$ be a natural number with $i+1\le w$, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a
machine state satisfying the following conditions: $n,a,X,P,T,Z,C,Q,E$ are zero; its
radius is $s$, width is $w$, and code bound is $2^w$; its source and target codes are
less than $2^w$, its midpoint is at most $2^w$, and its level is $i+1$; its
saved-endpoints stack is less than $2^{w(w-(i+1))}$ and its phase stack is less than
$2^{w-(i+1)}$. Suppose also that $M<2^w$ and $M_2\le 2^w$. Starting at label $a1F$ with
the source code replaced by the old midpoint $M$, the midpoint replaced by $M_2$, and
the popped endpoint set to the old source code, the machine can reach label $loop$ with
the midpoint increased from its original value by one and every other register equal to
its value in $\mathrm{st}$. Every configuration strictly before the endpoint has all
registers at most $2^{w^2}$ and satisfies the machine's validity condition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Preservation under midpoint update]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.setM}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.setM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St}
\difficulty{1}
Let $s,w,i$ be natural numbers, and let a machine state satisfy the invariant with
parameters $s,w,i$. If a natural number $M'$ satisfies $M'\le 2^w$, then replacing the
state's midpoint register by $M'$ leaves the invariant satisfied.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Equivalent bounded witnesses]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.exists_shift}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.exists_shift}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $R_1,R_2$ be predicates on natural numbers and let $a,K\in\mathbb{N}$. If it is not
the case that both $R_1(a)$ and $R_2(a)$ hold, then there exists an $m$ with $a+1\leq
m<K$ satisfying both predicates if and only if there exists an $m$ with $a\leq m<K$
satisfying both predicates.
\end{lemma}

\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.loop_spec}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b001}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.loop_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.refl, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.trans, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CallOK, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.setM, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.desc1, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.desc2, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.exists_shift, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail0F, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail1F, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.tail1T, Complexity.LogProg.astep}
\difficulty{6}
Let $E,s,w,i\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{O}$ be an oracle on four indices and bit
strings, and let $x$ be a bit string. Suppose $s\le w$, $i+1\le w$, and the
recursive-call property holds at level $i$. For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and register
state $\mathrm{st}$ satisfying the level-$(i+1)$ invariant and $\mathrm{st}.M+k=2^w$,
there is an $M'\le 2^w$ and a finite run, guarded by bound $2^{w^2}$ before its final
configuration, from label $\mathrm{loop}$ with registers $\mathrm{st}$ and no answer to
label $\mathrm{rt}(b)$ with registers equal to $\mathrm{st}$ except that $M=M'$, and no
answer, where $b$ is true exactly when there exists $m$ with $\mathrm{st}.M\le m<2^w$
such that the level-$i$ reachability relation holds from $\mathrm{st}.U$ to $m$ and from
$m$ to $\mathrm{st}.V$.
\end{theorem}

\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.CallOK, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv.setM, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.base_spec, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.loop_spec, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.step_of, Complexity.LogProg.astep}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E,s,w$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean oracle with four indices and
Boolean-word inputs, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean word. If $s\le w$, then for every
natural number $i\le w$ and every register state $\mathrm{st}$ satisfying the level-$i$
invariant for $s,w$, there is a natural number $M'\le 2^w$ such that the program $A(E)$
has a finite execution from label $\mathrm{cl}$, starting with register vector $\mathrm{st}$ and no
answer, to the return label whose Boolean value is the truth value of level-$i$
reachability from $\mathrm{st}.U$ to $\mathrm{st}.V$ with bound $2^w$ and relation determined by the
step oracle, $x$, and $s$. Every preterminal configuration satisfies the program guard
and has all registers at most $2^{w^2}$; the final register vector agrees with $\mathrm{st}$
except that its midpoint register is $M'$.
\end{theorem}
